sense: a sum of money; a total

terms.gloss: a sum, the total; a sum of money
terms.comment: The amount a reckoning comes to, counting every item (Lewis & Short); summa pecūniae, a sum of money.

phrases.latin: Quanta istaec hominum summast? — Septem mīlia.
phrases.english: What does that come to in men? — Seven thousand.

phrases.latin: addendō dēdūcendōque vidēre, quae reliquī summa fīat, ex quō, quantum cuique dēbeātur, intellegās
phrases.english: to see, by adding and subtracting, what the balance comes to, so that you understand how much is owed to each

sources: Lewis & Short: summa
Plautus, Miles gloriosus, and Cicero’s De officiis checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
